title: Stable smoothing with a prescribed ten-canonical projective frame
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $g\geq2$, and let $C/k$ be an unpointed stable genus-$g$ curve [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Put $r=19(g-1)$ and let a projective frame $\tau:\mathbf P(H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes10}))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be prescribed, using the dualizing-line and projective-frame conventions of [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter]. Let $R=k[[t]]$, $K=k((t))=R[1/t]$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. There exist a projective flat finitely presented unpointed stable genus-$g$ family $f:\mathcal C\to S$, an isomorphism $\mathcal C_k\simeq C$, and a projective frame $\widetilde\tau:\mathbf P(f_*\omega_{\mathcal C/R}^{\otimes10})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P^{r-1}_R$ restricting to $\tau$. The generic fibre $\mathcal C_K$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The frame gives a closed relative complete ten-canonical embedding, hence a morphism $\alpha:S\to J$ whose special point is the prescribed framed curve, where $J$ is the ten-canonical Hilbert parameter over $k$ from [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter]. Its generic embedded curve has degree $20(g-1)$ and genus $g$.

source.place: Stacks Tags 0E7Y (examples-defos.tex lemma-smoothing-proper-curve-isolated-lci), 0E76 (moduli-curves.tex lemma-stable-curves), 0E78 (lemma-stable-one-piece-per-genus); Morrison Section 3.3 Corollary 11(2), printed p.17, smoothing and framing. Agent synthesis; local Morrison PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], $C$ is flat and finitely presented over $k$, with nonempty reduced nodal geometric fibre of pure dimension one. Because $k$ is algebraically closed, $C$ itself is its geometric fibre. Its projective-bundle morphism is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] to $C/k$: its hypotheses of local finite type and equidimension one hold, and every closed point is smooth or a node by stability. We obtain that $C$ is a local complete intersection over $k$, and that its first-Fitting singular subscheme $Z$ is unramified over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0C4E, lemma-nodal-lci; properness: morphisms.tex Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], $|Z|$ is exactly the nonsmooth locus of $C/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-over-field-discrete], $|Z|$ is discrete. It is a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $|C|$, hence quasi-compact; its cover by singleton opens therefore has a finite subcover. Thus $C/k$ is smooth away from finitely many closed points (each singleton is closed in $Z$, and $Z$ is closed in $C$). The empty singular locus is allowed.

source.place: Tags 0C59, lemma-nodal-family, and 0C5B, lemma-base-change-nodal-family; morphisms.tex Tag 02G7, lemma-unramified-over-field

proof.text: The preceding steps verify all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-isolated-lci-curve-smoothing]: properness, the local complete-intersection condition, dimension at most one, and only finitely many nonsmooth points. It supplies a flat finitely presented projective $f:Y\to S=\operatorname{Spec}k[[t]]$, an isomorphism $Y_k\simeq C$, and smooth generic fibre $Y_K$. Retain this chosen special-fibre isomorphism throughout.

The family $Y/S$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fibre-dimension-upper-semicontinuous], the locus where its fibres have dimension at most one is open and contains the closed point, since $Y_k\simeq C$. $R=k[[t]]$ is local with maximal ideal $(t)$: a series is invertible exactly when its constant term is nonzero. An open of its spectrum containing the closed point is the whole spectrum: a basic open $D(a)$ inside it containing the maximal ideal has $a$ a unit, so $D(a)=S$. Thus every scheme-theoretic fibre $Y_s$ has dimension at most one. For a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ over $s$, every point of $Y_s\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\Omega$ has the same local fibre dimension as its image in $Y_s$ by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] ($Y\to S$ is of finite type); so every geometric fibre has dimension at most one. Apply [lem-sfb-stable-and-smooth-family-open-loci] to this proper flat finitely presented family. Its stable-genus-$g$ open contains the closed point and hence is all of $S$ by the same argument. Since this open is $S$, the identity of $S$ factors through it; its stated universal property now says that $f$ itself is an unpointed stable genus-$g$ family. Write $\mathcal C=Y$. Its generic fibre remains smooth.

source.place: Tags 0E76, lemma-stable-curves, and 0E78, lemma-stable-one-piece-per-genus; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0D4I, lemma-dimension-fibres-proper; morphisms.tex Tag 02FY, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change, part (1)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] to $f$: all geometric fibres are nonempty reduced pure-one-dimensional nodal curves, and $f$ is proper flat finitely presented. Its dualizing invertible module restricts to $\omega_C$ under our chosen special-fibre isomorphism: the cited compatibility with base change and with isomorphisms of families gives this identification for that chosen isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter] to this stable genus-$g$ family. The module $V=f_*\omega_{\mathcal C/R}^{\otimes10}$ is locally free of rank $r=19(g-1)$ and commutes with arbitrary base change. In particular $V\otimes_Rk\simeq H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes10})$, and evaluation gives a closed complete ten-canonical embedding $\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(V)$.

source.place: Tag 0E6R, lemma-gorenstein-dualizing; ten-canonical relative embedding as in the cited Hilbert-parameter node

proof.text: By the local-freeness definition [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], some open neighbourhood of the closed point trivializes $V$. This open is all of $S$ by the basic-open argument of step 4. Choose $V\simeq\mathcal O_S^r$ and let $\phi_0:\mathbf P_S(V)\simeq\mathbf P^{r-1}_S$ be its induced projective frame. Let $\phi_{0,k}$ denote its special-fibre frame, with the cohomological identification of step 5.

source.place: Tags 01C6 and 01C7, local-freeness definition; elementary local-spectrum argument

proof.text: The automorphism $a=\tau\circ\phi_{0,k}^{-1}$ of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ is induced by some $A\in\operatorname{GL}_r(k)$ by [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl]: its assertion that matrices represent projective automorphisms Zariski locally is global on the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Here $r\geq19$, so the cited hypothesis $r\geq2$ holds. Regard $A$ and its inverse as constant matrices over $R$ via $k\hookrightarrow k[[t]]$. The coefficient inclusion is a section of the residue map $R\to k$, so their matrix products remain the identity and their reductions are the original matrices. Thus they induce an automorphism $\widetilde a$ of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_R$ reducing to $a$. Set $\widetilde\tau=\widetilde a\circ\phi_0$. Then $\widetilde\tau_k=a\circ\phi_{0,k}=\tau$, exactly the prescribed frame.

source.place: Projective-bundle quotient convention, Tag 01OA; matrix lifting is the agent argument using the cited projective-automorphism statement

proof.text: Compose the closed complete embedding of step 5 with $\widetilde\tau$. The functor represented by $J$ in [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter] takes precisely a stable genus-$g$ family with this projective frame, so the pair defines $\alpha:S\to J$. Its reduction is the framed curve $(C,\tau)$ by steps 3 and 7. On the smooth generic stable fibre, [lem-sfb-stable-curve-pluricanonical-linear-series] at $n=10$ gives degree $10(2g-2)=20(g-1)$; its arithmetic genus is $g$ by step 4. All projectivity, flatness and finite-presentation conclusions were already supplied in step 3.
